items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep pr-cost on the trusted pre-merge version**

When the integrated PR modifies `scripts/orchestrator/pr-cost.sh`, the preceding `ff-main` step replaces the version that was checked against the trusted pre-merge `HEAD`; this line then executes the newly merged, PR-controlled script with the orchestrator's GitHub credentials. Preserve and execute the pre-merge copy, or otherwise verify the script again before invoking it after the fast-forward. This is trust-boundary code, and the declared control that repository scripts come from the trusted main checkout no longer mitigates the risk once that checkout has moved to the PR's commit.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L75-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/a8d975c68ba386da8541491faf5fdb2c23a8dcf2/AGENTS.md#L75-L78)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate the entire audit-finding disposition**

For a `Verdict: correct` summary, this prefix-only match accepts records such as `audit-finding: <sha7>:1 not-applicable:x`, even though the required reason must be substantive and the task's specified form includes evidence. Because `--audit-dispositions` is omitted for a correct verdict, neither `acceptance-front-matter.py` nor the gate subsequently validates this prose, so the closed audit-findings path can merge with a malformed disposition. Validate the complete line, including the minimum-length reason and required evidence delimiter, before resolving threads.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L75-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/72d0cd074ebd805cee9f343c849206b16137b650/AGENTS.md#L75-L78)

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Wait for the pull request to actually merge**

When `main` uses a merge queue, this command can return successfully after merely enqueueing the PR; `gh pr merge --help` explicitly says a passing PR is “added to the merge queue.” The immediate fetch can therefore still see the pre-merge `origin/main`, after which `ff-main` succeeds, `pr-cost` records an open PR, and the script emits an accepted `AGMSG-ACCEPTANCE` for a PR that has not merged. Poll the PR state and obtain its actual merge commit before continuing; binding the queued request to the audited head does not mitigate this merge-effect risk.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L78-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/9a918f8442368aba283099a16e379bf6a03634cd/AGENTS.md#L78-L78)

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Run ff-main with pre-merge resolved binaries**

When the caller's PATH contains mise shims and the merged PR changes `mise.toml`, starting the trusted `ff-main.sh` file is insufficient: after its `git merge --ff-only origin/main` updates the checkout, the script continues invoking bare `git`, `mkdir`, `cp`, and `rm`, whose shim resolution can now select PR-controlled tools with the orchestrator's credentials. Execute this step with a PATH of binaries resolved before the merge, as is already done for `pr-cost.sh`; the threat-table claim that the landed script is used does not close this environment-switch risk.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L75-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/8d09f80e53d9ae9482fec9aa551143565e7fa595/AGENTS.md#L75-L78)

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require the pull request base to be main**

If the PR is retargeted to another branch whose tip currently equals `origin/main`, the gate still accepts it because `pr_base_errors` returns success when the base SHA matches without requiring `baseRefName == main`. The installed `gh pr merge --help` states that `--squash` merges into the PR's base branch, so this command can merge that other branch; the subsequent main fetch and fast-forward then succeed as a no-op and the script emits an accepted result even though the audited change never reached main. Check the base ref explicitly before this merge.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L75-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/8d09f80e53d9ae9482fec9aa551143565e7fa595/AGENTS.md#L75-L78)
